note: arXiv abs 1610.02136 (Hendrycks & Gimpel; published at ICLR 2017). The abstract covers both misclassification and OOD detection, says correctly classified examples tend to have higher max softmax probability, and says the baseline can sometimes be surpassed. Both quotes match.

arXiv abs 2010.03759 (Liu et al., NeurIPS 2020). The abstract states the 18.03% reduction in average FPR at TPR 95% versus the softmax score, measured on a CIFAR-10 pretrained WideResNet. The setting matches the claim and is limited to that model and dataset, not a general result.

arXiv abs 2207.07506 (Xia & Bouganis, ACCV 2022, Best Paper). Both quotes match the abstract. The abstract does not name the baseline as MSP; 'softmax baseline' is the finding's own reading, consistent with the paper's SCOD setup. 'Generally fail' paraphrases 'fail to do so [consistently match or outperform]'.

Frontiers in Plant Science 2022 (peer-reviewed), doi 10.3389/fpls.2022.989086. Dataset: 8 known strawberry diseases plus unknowns, 13,089 images. Two-head AUROC 0.972 with unknown recall 94.9%; OpenMatch AUROC 0.971; OpenMax accuracy 70.1% (AUROC 0.812). Caveat: the 16.4% gain is OpenMatch with outliers (86.5%) minus OpenMax (70.1%). The authors admit these are structurally different methods, so this is a cross-method comparison, not a controlled ablation of outlier exposure.

Dong et al., Scientific Reports 14:17900 (2024), doi 10.1038/s41598-024-66958-2, peer-reviewed; checked the JBNU Pure abstract page. The abstract says five public datasets, VPT max-logit AUROC 94.8% at 8-shot, and full fine-tuning 95.2% on the full dataset. Caveat: the full text was not accessible (Nature/PMC blocked), so I could not confirm whether 94.8/95.2 is an average over all five datasets or a single-dataset figure. 'Across five datasets' may overstate.
